t: This is the South Bank Lion, a sculpture from 1837 that has stood beside County Hall, on the South Bank of the Thames, since 1966. It is a significant depiction of a lion, and is often mentioned alongside the four lions around Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square, just across the river. It was made by William Frederick Woodington, an English painter and sculptor who lived from 1806 to 1893. Take a moment to look at the lion's pose and the detail of the carving.
